decisions.why: FR-004 asks which tools and hooks read the records whole. The read counter observes the file reads of every command run under it in whatever language, so the Rust census is an instrument choice for finding candidates, not a narrowing of which tools count.

decisions.summary: Commands that push, archive or need a reviewer's reply are judged by their code and the in-process bench, not run.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks whether each reads a record whole; reading the code answers that, and the bench gives the cost of a whole read. Not running a command that pushes or archives from a measurement copy narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.id: T536-5 frequency from the day's logs
decisions.summary: How often each reader ran is counted from 2026-11-27's lines of the 451, 461, 462 and _unassigned event logs.
decisions.why: A before figure for a split the same day; FR-004 sets no window, and the day the records were whole is the window it needs.

decisions.id: T536-6 builder transcripts as the agents' reads
decisions.summary: Agents' own reads of 451's records are counted over the 146 builder transcripts of the day only; besides those, the only agent measured is one spec-fidelity plan-review dispatch, and that reading is of the tool it runs, not of the agent's own Read calls.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks which agents read the records whole, and SC-002 then holds that no reader named in the before figure reads a record whole after the split. Counting builders only leaves every other agent type's own reads unmeasured: the reviewers, the verify twins, the arbiter, escalation-check, the process reviewer and the coordinating session. Those agents are then never 'named there', so SC-002 passes for them without anyone having looked. Counting them is not impossible: the same script (t536-builder-reads.py) runs over those transcripts. The GM's own words in the bundle do not imply the exclusion, since request.md line 525 says only 'doing the split that we discussed' and the cited messages are not in the bundle. Keeping the exclusion therefore defeats the before figure's purpose for those agents. Fix: run the same script over the day's other agent transcripts, with a dated method line, and record what it finds, or record that they read none of the four records.

decisions.id: T536-7 found and left as costs
decisions.summary: plan-delta's repeated reads (2.6 s a call) and task-time's 260 s a call are classed as costs, not defects, and filed in 462 as T543 and T544.
decisions.why: Constitution XIV: a defect is a wrong outcome; a slow but correct command is a cost. 462 FR-001 sends a task filed from now on to 462. D15 passes a 'not a defect' item without an order.

decisions.summary: T536 is counted as performance work, a measurement of where time and context go.
decisions.why: FR-013: measurement of where the time goes counts as performance work for ordering (the GM, 2026-11-20).

decisions.id: T536-9 after figure by the same scripts
decisions.summary: T537's after figure is read with the same scripts, which match paths by directory so a split record's parts are counted.
decisions.why: SC-002 needs the before and after figures to be comparable; using the same instrument does that and narrows nothing.

### T536 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: T532's two blocks are the unfilled template: every field a placeholder, no approach, no step row.
decisions.why: A placeholder decides nothing, so it narrows nothing the request or 462 FR-001 (which keeps T532 in the closing set) asks. This CLEAR rules only that no decision in these blocks narrows the request. It is not a ruling that T532's work was planned or matches its line.

decisions.summary: T536 is a read-only measurement on copies of the records taken at 20:03:07Z, written up in dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t536-record-readers/results.md, with no source changes.
decisions.why: 462 FR-004 asks T536 to MEASURE which tools, hooks and agents read the large records whole while they are whole, before T537 splits them. Measuring on copies of the records while they are whole is exactly that. Changing no source is the brief and leaves the split to T537.

decisions.summary: The 'large records' are four: plan-review.json, plan-done.md, tasks-done.md and the event log, each sized and hashed in the snapshot.
decisions.why: FR-004 says '451's large records' without listing them. The four named are the large ones by the measured sizes (0.6 MB to 54 MB), and the plan says which they are rather than leaving it open.

decisions.summary: Tools and hooks are found two ways. The census is of non-test Rust lines naming a record or its constant or helper (285 lines, search space stated). Bytes per call are counted by an LD_PRELOAD read counter on the built binaries. land, tick, carry and plan-verdict are given by reading the code, because they push, archive or need a reviewer, and their cost comes from the bench.
decisions.why: This answers FR-004's 'which tools and hooks' for every reader the census names. The read counter follows the commands' child processes, so a reader in any language behind a measured command is counted. Taking four commands from code because they cannot safely be run on a copy is a choice of method, stated in item 4. It drops none of them from the answer.

decisions.summary: Agents' reads come from the day's transcripts. Builders are counted separately (146 transcripts). Every other agent type and the session are counted with ALL=1. The result: which types read a large record, how many bytes, and that none read one whole (the largest read is 28,207 bytes).
decisions.why: This carries FR-004's 'agents', which the version last judged covered only for builders. The window is one day, the day the figure is taken, and it is stated. Token figures are marked ESTIMATE.

decisions.summary: Adds claims-triage, plan-section, where-time and feature-report, measured with the read counter: none, once for a finished task's section, three times and five times whole.
decisions.why: These extend the census of tools to the readers the earlier round asked about. That is more of FR-004's own measurement, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Two costs are left as 'not a defect' and filed in 462 as performance levers: plan-delta reads plan-done.md 11 times a call (2.6 s), and task-time takes 260 s a call. They are T543 and T544.
decisions.why: A slow call that gives a correct answer is a cost, not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV as the GM stated it on 2026-11-19), so the D15 deferral form does not apply. Filing new work in 462 rather than 451 is what 462 FR-001 orders. Nothing the request asks of T536 is left undone.

decisions.summary: T536 runs before T537 while the records are whole. The after figure is read later with the same scripts, which match paths by directory so a split record's parts are counted.
decisions.why: This is 462 FR-004's order and SC-002's 'before figure recorded before T537 lands', with the means to read the after figure the same way.

blocks: ### T535 (the batch gate of 2026-11-27 19:10Z failed T364's late-reader test once on good work; the round arbiter's ruling on red-gate@2026-11-27T19:10:08Z: a defect in the test or the drain, found red first)
### T535 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.id: T535-D1 locate the defect in the drain
decisions.summary: The false red is put in rustc/drain.rs's holders, which counted a sibling thread's spawn caught between its fork and its exec as a holder of the late pipe. The test is kept as it is.
decisions.why: The arbiter's ruling (red-gate@2026-11-27T19:10:08Z, quoted in the block heading) is that the defect is in the test or the drain and must be found red first. The GM's 2026-11-26 words in request.md on the test that fails under load ('I agree with prioritizing the test that fails under load being fixed') and the fix-as-we-go rule both call for fixing a check that refuses good work. Fixing the root cause in the drain, rather than relaxing the test, keeps the test's job intact.

decisions.summary: A new test parks a child in the fork-to-exec window past DRAIN with pre_exec, and the child signals that it is there. On the old code it failed 3 of 3 runs and took the existing no-holder test down with it.
decisions.why: This is enforcement of the fix the arbiter ruled must be found red first. If the fix is deleted the test fails, so it is verification and not new behavior.

decisions.summary: A process is not counted as a holder when its parent is this process and its /proc/<pid>/exe is this process's program, i.e. a spawn that has forked but not yet exec'd.
decisions.why: This is the fix itself. It narrows nothing the GM asked for. T363's leak pin and T364's drain are stated as unchanged, and a real holder (any exec'd process, or anything not a child of this program) is still counted. The soundness premise ('nothing under this program runs a copy of itself') is a design claim. It is not a narrowing of the request.

decisions.summary: ended counts a holder only if it is found twice, AGAIN apart (50 ms, a GUESS knob, paid only when a pipe is still held at DRAIN), as left.rs does with GRACE. This closes the gap where the exe is renamed just before begin_new_exec drops close-on-exec descriptors.
decisions.why: Part of the same fix, closing a race in the skip rule. It is labeled a GUESS knob. It costs 50 ms only on a real leak's HELD line, and the block states that cost (checklist item 12). It is not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.id: T535-D5 not performance work, found-and-left none, one landing
decisions.summary: Classed as a false-red fix, not performance work. Nothing found and left. Budget of one landing. Ordered after T364 and T363.
decisions.why: A gate check that refuses good work is a defect to fix as it is found. Nothing is deferred, so no narrowing arises. Ordering after the tasks whose code it changes is mechanical.

blocks: ### T537 (462 FR-004 and SC-002, the GM's go of 2026-11-27, "doing the split that we discussed", on future sessions "naively just opening these very large files and then blowing through their own context windows": 451's finished records cut into parts a reader of one task can open safely, every tool that reads them pointed at the new layout)
### T537 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The archive layout: archive/plan-done and archive/tasks-done parts each with a header, archive/index.json, and archive/INDEX.md, a reader's note saying what is where, how to find one task, and warning off whole reads, cat archive/* and broad greps; an unsplit feature reads its flat files as before.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'mechanically split up the large files into smaller files' with notes 'cautioning future sessions ... to avoid like wrecking their context usage', and it names his grep worry. One gap: the GM asked for notes 'explaining what we did and why' as well as cautioning, and the block lists where things are, the lookup route and the warning, but not the why: that the split was made because sessions were blowing their context windows. One sentence in INDEX.md closes that. Not a narrowing of the request's purpose.

decisions.summary: The cut: pieces at ## / ### headings and column-0 boxes, taken in runs in the record's own order, packed under BOUND = 65,536 bytes (a GUESS knob); a run larger than BOUND stands alone.
decisions.why: How the mechanical split is done, which the request and spec leave open. The record-order choice keeps make plan-section's output as before (observed by the plan, one-shot label). Aside, not a ruling: the goal line says 'at most 64 KiB' but the largest part is 65,652 bytes with its header, and a run larger than BOUND stands alone, so that line should say 'about 64 KiB' or name the exception.

decisions.summary: The fold runs unforced at every tick and in make plan-archive, ONLY where archive/ already stands; no other feature is split unasked; a size trigger is left to 462 T546; a failed tick commit's put-back cleans the feature's archive/.
decisions.why: The GM spoke of 'this feature', meaning 451's records, and 462 FR-004 names 451's records. Folding new ticks into parts keeps the split records split. Splitting other features automatically was not asked, so leaving the size trigger to T546 narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Every reader of the flat records is repointed through archive.rs (done_text and its callers, plan_done, plan-section reading only the task's parts, task-add's next id from the index, builder-tree, the queue, the feature-approval guard, started-answers, spec-lint over the parts); some are left by judgment because they hold names, not reads, or never read the flat records.
decisions.why: 'Every tool that reads them pointed at the new layout' is what the split needs to work. Keeping the readers' outputs as they were is what 'everything works' means here, and no exactness standard is applied.

decisions.summary: Readers whose job is the whole set (make plan-delta, make decide, stale-terms) are left reading every part as often as they read the flat file; their cost is filed in 462 as T543 and T547 and called a cost, not a defect.
decisions.why: LEGITIMATE against SC-002's 'no reader named there reads a record whole'. A mechanical cut cannot make a reader whose job needs every task read less, so the literal rule is physically impossible for these readers. The bytes stay inside a tool process and do not reach a session's context window, which is the harm the GM named. Ruled on the plan's own statement of what these readers do; T536's named list is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: make task-add's quick now reads the plan-done parts four times (14.7 MB) where it read the flat plan-done.md not at all; filed as 462 T547 and called a cost, not a defect.
decisions.why: LEGITIMATE, but recorded. This is a read the split ADDS, not one it leaves. It contradicts block 1's statement that the readers left by judgment each read 'what it read before', and the plan should say which check now reads the parts and why. Under constitution XIV it is a cost, not a wrong outcome: the bytes stay in-process and do not reach a session's context, and it is filed. It does not block. If that check now RULES on archived text it used to skip (refusing or flagging good work), that would be a defect, and the plan should state that it does not.

decisions.summary: The third of FR-004's records, plan-review.json (5.0 MB, observed 2026-11-27, the largest), is not split by T537 and is carried by 462 T545, because its readers parse it as one JSON record and a split changes the plan crate's record rather than cutting text. INDEX.md is not said to warn a session off it meanwhile.
decisions.why: NOT LEGITIMATE. 462 FR-004 assigns the split of 451's large records to T537, and the plan itself counts three records and splits two. The stated reason, that its readers parse one JSON record so a split changes the plan crate, is 'harder to implement, needs more of the codebase changed'. That is on the not-legitimate list: a JSON record can be split, so it is not impossible. Nothing in the GM's words excludes it, and doing it literally does not defeat his purpose. On purpose, this is the largest file, exactly the one a future session 'naively just opening these very large files' would hit. A filed task in another feature is not a legitimizer, and T545's text and order are not in the bundle. Two things clear this: (a) T537 splits plan-review.json, or the third record is moved to 462 T545 by an amendment to 462's spec (FR-004's T537 assignment) or by an arbiter ruling; and in either case (b) INDEX.md, or a note beside plan-review.json, warns sessions off reading it whole NOW, which costs nothing and need not wait for the split.

decisions.summary: The real 451 records are not split in T537's push. The session runs make archive-split F=451 once T537's code is on main and commits the flat files' deletions and archive/. The after figure is measured on a copy.
decisions.why: LEGITIMATE as sequencing. The readers must be on main before the flat files go, or an older guard binary in the mirror reads a missing file. The records also keep changing until 451's closing set lands, so a deletion committed in the same push would conflict. This is a real ordering constraint, not a preference. The 'advisor's ruling' is given no weight; the ordering reason stands on its own. The split still happens. The plan should make that run a tracked step, a ticked task or the exit's green condition, rather than a sentence, so T537 cannot be ticked and the split forgotten.

decisions.summary: make feature-report's tasks_done and tick times, and make where-time's tick windows, read the split layout (done_text, and git log -p over archive/tasks-done beside the flat file); pinned in feature_report/sources/tests.rs.
decisions.why: A defect the split would cause, a wrong ticked count, fixed in the same task. That is the 'fix as we go' rule and part of 'every tool pointed at the new layout'.

decisions.summary: The owed tests (the tick's fold, plan-archive's fold Err, task-add's index closure, spec-lint over a part, started-answers and the feature-approval guard at a split base, builder-tree and the queue on a split dir, a part with no header, and a landing of a split feature) are written in the closing half.
decisions.why: Tests whose only effect is making the requested split work and keep working. That is enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope.
